purpose: Validate, inspect, deterministically compile, and materialize renderer-neutral visual asset packages made from exact reusable atoms for shape, parts, textures, materials, palettes, gradients, masks, overlays, shaders, animations, states, behavior, LOD, collision, sockets, and metadata.

properties.operation: one of inspect-schema, list, inspect, validate, compile, or materialize
properties.ref: optional exact installed asset package id@version; required for inspect and mutually exclusive with package for validate, compile, and materialize
properties.package: optional inline axm.asset-atom-package/v0.1 object; mutually exclusive with ref
properties.atom_kind: optional exact list filter from the closed v0.1 atom-kind set
properties.observation_distance: optional finite non-negative distance used for exact LOD selection
properties.palette_overrides: optional palette-id to existing-role to color map
properties.path: required materialization directory outside the live machine body or under creations/
properties.replace: optional explicit boolean replacement of an existing creation target

relationships: binds previously separate visual concepts into one exact reusable package grammar
lets finished assets be deterministic dependency graphs of smaller reusable visual atoms
keeps external media, runtime shader behavior, animation playback, and physics execution distinct from descriptor validation
coexists with Paintgun and Chameleon without claiming the current SVG renderer is a 3D runtime

anatomy_refs.basis: Texture atoms declare bounded channel and resource descriptors.
Mask atoms attach explicit meanings to texture components.
Gradient atoms carry exact stops and optional palette roles.
Shape atoms can describe external mesh resources while leaving their bytes unclaimed.
Part children and socket transforms form explicit attachment topology.
Collision atoms stay separate from visible geometry.
LOD atoms enforce continuous non-overlapping distance coverage.
Material atoms bind scalar, color, texture, shader, palette, mask, gradient, and overlay inputs.
Animation atoms declare bounded tracks and strictly ordered keyframes.
State and behavior atoms declare exact transitions and selections without executing them.

limitations: the capability validates and compiles renderer-neutral JSON descriptors; it does not render mesh, sprite, vector, or texture content
shader instructions are not executed and custom runtime source is not trusted or run
animation clips and behaviors are selected but not played
collision shapes are validated but no collision or physics simulation is run
external resource bytes are not fetched or verified; supplied digests remain declared evidence only
the installed modular tank is a complete schema demonstrator, not a claim that its referenced media bytes exist
persistent_state: the installed read-only asset-packages body plus only caller-selected materialized creation directories

truth.basis: Closed fields, exact references, kind checks, cycle rejection, deterministic digests, and explicit resource/runtime limits prevent descriptor claims from becoming runtime claims.

agency.basis: Every atom, dependency, variant, palette role, socket, and selection stays inspectable and independently replaceable.

continuity.basis: Installed packages are versioned local source and materialization writes ordinary validated creations without changing the live machine body.

wisdom-before-speed.basis: Invalid, ambiguous, cyclic, discontinuous, or wrongly typed compositions fail closed before materialization.
